title: Configuration and secrets
summary: One image for every environment: configure with environment variables, and keep secrets out of images.

steps.title: Build once, configure per environment
body: The image you tested is the image you ship. It must not be rebuilt for staging or production; **configuration comes from the environment** at run time (one of the "twelve-factor app" rules).
.NET reads environment variables on top of `appsettings.json`, and `__` maps to `:`:
Keys are case-insensitive. Node apps read `process.env.X`; the idea is the same everywhere.

steps.prompt: Match each environment variable to the .NET configuration key it sets.

steps.title: Secrets never go in the image
body: Anyone who can pull an image can read **every layer**, and `docker history` shows every instruction:
ENV DB_PASSWORD=hunter2              # baked into the image config forever
ARG NPM_TOKEN                        # build args show up in docker history
COPY .env .                          # the file is in a layer, even if a later RUN deletes it

- **At run time**, inject secrets from the platform: Compose/Swarm `secrets:` (mounted as files under `/run/secrets/`), Kubernetes Secrets, a cloud key vault. Environment variables are acceptable for many teams, but files are not visible in `docker inspect`.
- **At build time** (a private package feed token), use a BuildKit secret mount, which exists only during that one `RUN` and is never written to a layer:

steps.prompt: A Dockerfile has `COPY .npmrc .`, then `RUN npm ci && rm .npmrc`. Is the token safe?
options: No: the COPY layer still contains .npmrc; deleting it later only hides it in the final filesystem
Yes: the file was deleted before the image was finished
Yes, as long as the image is pushed to a private registry
No, but only because npm logs the token
steps.explain: Layers are additive. Use `RUN --mount=type=secret,...` so the file never lands in a layer.

steps.prompt: Does the secret end up readable by someone who pulls the image?
Use a private NuGet feed during `dotnet restore` without leaving the credentials in any layer.
Which configuration key does a .NET app see for this variable? Type the key.

steps.title: Effective configuration, safely printed
prompt: Write `List<string> Effective(Dictionary<string, string> json, Dictionary<string, string> env)` that prints a .NET app's effective configuration for a startup log.
1. Start from `json` (keys already flattened with `:`, like `ConnectionStrings:Default`).
2. Apply each `env` entry on top, with `__` replaced by `:`. Keys are **case-insensitive**: when an env key matches an existing key, the value changes but the original spelling of the key is kept.
3. Return `KEY = VALUE` lines sorted by key (case-insensitive ordinal).

4. Never print secrets: if the key contains `password`, `secret` or `token` (any case), print `***` as the value; otherwise, if the value contains `Password=`, replace everything after it up to the next `;` (or the end) with `***`.
starter: List<string> Effective(Dictionary<string, string> json, Dictionary<string, string> env)
var config = new Dictionary<string, string>(json, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
solution: List<string> Effective(Dictionary<string, string> json, Dictionary<string, string> env)
var config = new Dictionary<string, string>(json, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
foreach (var kv in env) config[kv.Key.Replace("__", ":")] = kv.Value;
foreach (string key in config.Keys.OrderBy(k => k, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
template: Dojo.Eq("env overrides, secrets masked", new List<string> { "ConnectionStrings:Default = Host=db;Database=shop;Password=***", "Jwt:SigningSecret = ***", "Logging:LogLevel:Default = Warning", "Smtp:Host = mail" }, Effective(dojoJson, dojoEnv));

Dojo.Eq("json only", new List<string> { "ConnectionStrings:Default = Host=localhost;Password=***;Database=shop", "Jwt:SigningSecret = ***", "Logging:LogLevel:Default = Information" }, Effective(dojoJson, new Dictionary<string, string>()));

Dojo.Eq("token key", new List<string> { "Api:Token = ***", "Api:Url = https://x" }, Effective(new Dictionary<string, string>(), new Dictionary<string, string> { ["Api__Url"] = "https://x", ["Api__Token"] = "abc" }));
hints: A dictionary created with `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase` keeps the first spelling of a key when you assign through the indexer.
Mask by key name first; only look inside the value when the key is not secret.
